summary: Join Adaptive Management for Complex Humanitarian Projects Course. Gain essential tools and insights to effectively manage and adapt in challenging environments
lede: Adaptive management helps humanitarian teams adjust programmes as context, access, and community priorities change. For programme, MEAL, response, and grants professionals, the course builds practical skills to spot change signals, test assumptions, set adaptation triggers, document justified adjustments, and review outcomes using evidence, feedback workflows, and indicator dashboards.
audienceIntro: Adaptive management for humanitarian projects is suited to professionals who make, support, monitor, or govern programme decisions in complex operating environments. It is appropriate for experienced practitioners who need a stronger bridge between field evidence, programme controls, and accountable adaptation.
prerequisites: You should have practical experience in humanitarian programme delivery, MEAL, grants management, response coordination, protection, cash programming, or programme quality. A working knowledge of results frameworks, indicators, risk registers, and project review meetings is expected. No programming is required. Advanced concepts such as PDIA, Cynefin, outcome harvesting, and AI-assisted qualitative synthesis are taught at conceptual and operational application level, while dashboard, decision-log, and roadmap activities provide guided hands-on practice.
